1999.label: NBA Live 99
1999.name: The NLSC
1999.terms: 'NBA Live 99 Original 1998 Rosters' 1.0 (8 March 2017, uploaded by Andrew) from the NLSC's Downloads database: EA's own roster files from the NBA Live 99 PC CD-ROM (© EA Sports 1998), no licence given. The .7z (MD5 6280cd1d87748d80689c053037c028e0) is pinned as downloaded, and its PLAYERS.DBF and TEAMS.DBF as extracted; only those two dBase tables are read, as data. Because of the 1998 lockout the game shipped with the final 1997/98 rosters plus the trades of May and June 1998 and none of the 1998 draft; the season is 1998/99, the edition's, as NBA 2K12 carries 2011/12 on the lockout's 2010/11 rosters. Free agents and the All-Star teams are left out, and so is every player Basketball-Reference (check) does not have playing in the NBA: the made-up 'Roster Player' and a draft pick who never played. Each player keeps EA's computed overall (OVERALLRTG) as `raw`, put on NBA 2K's scale by `scale`.

scale.note: NBA Live 99's overall is the rounded mean of 17 of its ratings, so it runs low (28-71 here) and undervalues specialists. One straight line puts it on NBA 2K's scale: the least-squares line of NBA 2K's overall (2K Archive's NBA 2K, 1999/00) on NBA Live 99's, through the players both editions rate, matched by name or alias. rating = round(20.22 + 1.089 × raw); its slope is positive, so no player passes another. The build fits the line again and stops if it is not this one. The audit gives every raw overall's rating and how the line does on those players.

2012.name: The Real 2K Insider
2012.terms: The pinned copy is the Wayback Machine's capture of 14 October 2011 (the live page's markup changes from one fetch to the next; its list does not). A fan blog with no licence; its ratings are 2K's launch ratings, transcribed from 2K's ratings video, on the lockout's launch rosters (the 2010/11 teams), as 2K Archive's are. 2K Archive lists only 3 Philadelphia and San Antonio players for NBA 2K12, so the season comes from this list whole; the audit counts how many of 2K Archive's players it rates the same.

check.name: Basketball-Reference's player seasons (Sumitro Datta, NBA Stats (1947-present), version 57)
check.terms: CC0: Public Domain, compiled from Basketball-Reference's regular seasons (dataset updated 1 November 2026). Read only to check facts: who played for which club in which season, and for how long. `codes` maps the manifest's team codes to Basketball-Reference's where they differ; `rotation` is the minutes a season's real player must have played for his club for the audit to name him if a source does not list him.

computed.label: Basketball-Reference (computed)
computed.name: Sumitro Datta, NBA Stats (1947-present), Kaggle, CC0, version 57
computed.terms: CC0: Public Domain (Kaggle's metadata), Sumitro Datta's copy of Basketball-Reference's regular seasons, dataset version 57 (updated 1 November 2026), downloaded anonymously from Kaggle's API; nothing was fetched from basketball-reference.com. PER, defensive win shares and SRS are Basketball-Reference's own calculations; Sports-Reference's data-use terms forbid scraping that harms its sites, building a competing database and AI training with its data, and say facts are not copyrightable. Advanced.csv gives each player season's position, games, minutes, PER and DWS; Player Totals.csv points and assists (the same file `check` pins); All-Star Selections.csv and End of Season Teams.csv the All-Star and All-NBA picks; Player Career Info.csv the career position (G, F-C...), for a player a season lists no position for and for a second position his other seasons do not give; Team Summaries.csv each team's name (checked against `teams`), its games (the minutes share's), its record and SRS (each club's move toward its results) and the league's pace and offensive rating, and Team Stats Per Game.csv its points a game (both checked against src/data/nbaLeagueAverages.js).

score.note: score = intercept + the sum of each coefficient times its input (docs/design/computed-ratings.md, step 3). Production: PER (a rate a minute), points, assists and defensive win shares a game, each pooled over the season and the one before it, weighted 3:1 (`window`, the user's choice of 2026-11-18 for the NBA over the method's 3:2:1, which every check measured worse: Σ weight × events / Σ weight × exposure, a season not played adding nothing), and shrunk toward the season's replacement level (the pooled rate of the quarter of its players with the least exposure) by a prior k = n̄(1 - rel) / rel × 3, rel the rate's rank correlation between the season and the one before among players with a quarter of each season's games, n̄ their mean exposure: measured each season, never set by hand. Selection: the share of his club's minutes he played (minutes / (48 × the club's games)), pooled the same way. Honours: All-Star (1 if picked) and All-NBA (3, 2 or 1 for the 1st, 2nd or 3rd team), the season's own. The coefficients are the least-squares fit of NBA 2K's overall, as a z-score within each edition, on those inputs as of each player's season before (2K rates a season's players from the season before), over 2K Archive's NBA 2K (1999/00) to NBA 2K26 (2025/26), its NBA 2K12 its own, players matched by name (and club where two share one): 9,970 pairs. Every coefficient is positive. The build fits them again and stops if any differs at six significant figures; the ratings use these, so a later copy of 2K Archive's page cannot move them.

computed.rule: Each season, each club's 13 players with the most minutes are rated (a traded player counts once, for the club he played the most minutes for). The league is ranked by score, and the player at rank quantile (rank - 0.5) / N takes NBA 2K27's rating at that quantile of its ratings of each club's 13 best (2K Archive, 390 ratings from 69 to 97, `spread.counts`; the build stops if the page's differ): no player passes another. A player's positions are the season's, else the first his career position implies (`positions`); the second is the neighbouring one he was listed at in other seasons with the most minutes, else the one his career position implies. A player with no position is left out. Then, by the user's decision of 2026-11-17 (docs/design/computed-ratings.md, step 5), each club moves toward its real results: its target is μ + √r × SRS / m, μ the season's mean strength before the move (the engine's strength of each club's five, selectLineup's), SRS Basketball-Reference's, r = 1 - (σ² / games) / Var(SRS) its reliability (an approximation: the copy keeps no games; σ, the game-margin spread, is fitted to the records of all the computed seasons at once), and m the match engine's margin a lineup point under the season's rules, measured by simulation on a generator seeded by the season. Every player of the club moves by one whole number and its best few (by rating, then score) one more, whichever brings its five nearest the target; no player passes a teammate.
